title: Why fields are hidden rather than overridden
answer: Fields are not polymorphically overridden. A subclass may declare a field with the same name, but that hides the parent field; field access is resolved using the declared type of the reference. Instance methods are different because eligible overridden methods participate in dynamic dispatch. Therefore parent-typed and child-typed references to the same object can read different same-named fields while an overridden method call still dispatches to the child.
